title: 184. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Linear Equations with No or Infinitely Many Solutions
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify when a linear equation has no solution.
questions.question: For a linear equation written as \(ax+b=cx+d\), under which condition does it have no solution?
questions.explanation:
Subtract \(cx\) from both sides, then subtract \(b\) from both sides and factor out \(x\):
\[
ax+b-cx=d \implies (a-c)x=d-b
\]
If \(a=c\), the equation becomes \(0=d-b\). When \(b\ne d\), this statement is false, so no value of \(x\) satisfies the equation. Therefore, the equation has no solution.
questions.hint: Rearrange the equation into the form \(Ax=B\) and compare the coefficient of \(x\) with the constant term.

questions.learningObjective: Identify when a linear equation has infinitely many solutions.
questions.question: For \(ax+b=cx+d\), which condition gives infinitely many solutions?
questions.explanation:
Rearranging gives
\[
(a-c)x=d-b
\]
If \(a=c\) and \(b=d\), then both sides become \(0\), so
\[
0=0
\]
is true for every value of \(x\). Therefore, the equation has infinitely many solutions.
questions.hint: An equation with infinitely many solutions must reduce to a true statement for every value of the variable.

questions.concept: Recognizing No Solution from an Equation
questions.learningObjective: Determine the number of solutions of \(2x+3=2x+7\).
questions.question: How many solutions does \(2x+3=2x+7\) have?
questions.explanation:
Subtract \(2x\) from both sides:
\[
3=7
\]
This statement is false, so no value of \(x\) satisfies the equation. Therefore, the equation has no solution.
questions.hint: Subtract the variable term from both sides and examine the remaining statement.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the number of solutions of \(3(x+2)=3x+6\).
questions.question: How many solutions does \(3(x+2)=3x+6\) have?
questions.explanation:
Distribute on the left side:
\[
3x+6=3x+6
\]
Both sides are identical, so the equation is true for every real value of \(x\). Therefore, it has infinitely many solutions.
questions.hint: Simplify each side and compare whether the two sides are identical.

questions.concept: Finding Parameter for Infinitely Many Solutions
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(k\) so that \(kx+4=5x+4\) has infinitely many solutions.
questions.question: What value of \(k\) makes \(kx+4=5x+4\) have infinitely many solutions?
questions.explanation:
Subtract \(4\) from both sides, then subtract \(5x\) from both sides:
\[
\begin{aligned}
kx &= 5x\\
(k-5)x &= 0
\end{aligned}
\]
For the equation to be true for every value of \(x\), the coefficient of \(x\) must be zero:
\[
\begin{aligned}
k-5 &= 0\\
k &= 5
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct value is \(k=5\).
questions.hint: For infinitely many solutions, the coefficient of \(x\) must equal zero after rearranging.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(m\) so that \(3x+m=3x-2\) has no solution.
questions.question: Which value of \(m\) makes \(3x+m=3x-2\) have no solution?
questions.explanation:
Subtract \(3x\) from both sides:
\[
m=-2
\]
If \(m=-2\), the equation becomes
\[
3x-2=3x-2
\]
which is true for all \(x\), so it has infinitely many solutions. If \(m=0\), the equation becomes
\[
3x=3x-2
\]
which simplifies to \(0=-2\), a false statement. Therefore, \(m=0\) gives no solution.
questions.hint: Subtract the variable term, then test whether the remaining constant statement is false.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the number of solutions of \(4x-8=4(x-2)\).
questions.question: How many solutions does \(4x-8=4(x-2)\) have?
questions.explanation:
Expand the right side:
\[
4(x-2)=4x-8
\]
Thus the equation becomes
\[
4x-8=4x-8
\]
Both sides are identical, so the equation is true for every real value of \(x\). Therefore, it has infinitely many solutions.
questions.hint: Expand the right side and compare it with the left side.

questions.concept: Conditions for No Solution with Parameters
questions.question: For \(ax+1=3x+b\), which condition gives no solution?
questions.explanation:
Rearrange the equation:
\[
\begin{aligned}
ax+1 &= 3x+b\\
(a-3)x &= b-1
\end{aligned}
\]
If \(a=3\) and \(b\ne 1\), then
\[
0=b-1
\]
is false, so the equation has no solution. If \(a=3\) and \(b=1\), the equation becomes \(0=0\), which gives infinitely many solutions.
questions.hint: Move all \(x\)-terms to one side and all constant terms to the other side.

questions.concept: Finding Parameter for Infinitely Many Solutions
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(k\) so that \(k(x+1)=4x+4\) has infinitely many solutions.
questions.question: What value of \(k\) makes \(k(x+1)=4x+4\) have infinitely many solutions?
questions.explanation:
Expand the left side:
\[
kx+k=4x+4
\]
For the equation to be true for every value of \(x\), the coefficients of \(x\) and the constant terms must both match:
\[
k=4
\]
Thus, the equation becomes
\[
4x+4=4x+4
\]
which is true for all \(x\). Therefore, the correct value is \(k=4\).
questions.hint: Expand first, then compare both the coefficient of \(x\) and the constant term.

questions.learningObjective: Determine conditions on \(a\) and \(b\) for infinitely many solutions of \((a-1)x+5=3x+b\).
questions.question: For \((a-1)x+5=3x+b\), what conditions give infinitely many solutions?
questions.explanation:
Rearrange the equation:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(a-1)x+5 &= 3x+b\\
(a-4)x &= b-5
\end{aligned}
\]
For infinitely many solutions, the equation must reduce to \(0=0\), so both sides must be zero. Thus \(a-4=0\) and \(b-5=0\), which gives \(a=4\) and \(b=5\). Therefore, the correct condition is \(a=4\) and \(b=5\).
questions.hint: After rearranging, both the coefficient of \(x\) and the constant term must be zero for an identity.
